headline: MGAT Alpha closed 15 trades this week for -$150.03 (40.00% win rate), a sharp reversal from last week's +$114.02. Nearly all of the loss traces to a single DEX position that lost 99.99% of its cost within about an hour of opening on a family-default beta -- pull that one trade out and the week is close to breakeven. BC and L1 both posted modestly positive weeks on their own merits while MED went 0-for-4 on ordinary exits. Measured-beta coverage of new positions rose to 78.57%, but it was the family-default fallback, not the measured share, that drove this week's loss. The sample (34 of a 200-trade target) is still far too small to call the logic healthy or broken, and two data-quality questions carried from prior weeks -- an idle counterfactual ledger and a symbol repeatedly flagged against the same witness price -- remain open.
llm_adviser: No new restart events this week -- the run has not rebooted since launch, and both boot records still read llm_mode: 'active'. It remains UNCONFIRMED whether this reflects the intended adviser switch (agreed state: OFF) or an unrelated runtime flag; unverified against source for a third consecutive week, so treat it as an open question rather than a settled OFF.
sample_caveat: 15 closed trades this week, 34 all-time against the 200-trade target -- about 17% of the way to a sample size worth treating as meaningful. Win rate (40.00% week, 38.24% all-time) and PnL% are still not a fully reliable read at this size: this week alone moved the all-time win rate by less than two points, but a single trade moved the all-time realized PnL by more than the entire prior four weeks combined. Directional at best.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper -- simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: No CLASS-A changes landed this week -- clean comparison. Two data-quality threads remain open from prior weeks and are unresolved for a second week running: the counterfactual ledger has recorded zero closes across its entire history, with its oldest positions now thirteen days old -- past the primary book's own seven-day time-stop horizon -- and one symbol has now been flagged twice against an identical witness price. Neither is a repair-log item; both are mechanism and data questions carried forward rather than resolved.

verdict.text: Taken at face value this looks like a losing week (-$150.03, 40.00% win rate, down from last week's turnaround), but the real story is narrower: pull out one DEX position that lost 99.99% of its cost within about an hour of opening on a family-default beta, and the week is close to breakeven. That doesn't excuse the trade -- a fresh position losing effectively all of its cost that fast is exactly the tail risk a conservative default beta is supposed to guard against by sizing down uncertainty, not into it, and that family's default beta deserves a look. Separately, BC and L1 both had genuinely decent weeks on their own merits while MED swept 0-for-4 on ordinary exits -- not a fault, just a bad week for that family. No CLASS-A changes landed and there was only one non-critical alarm, so this wasn't an operationally rough week either. What keeps this from 'healthy' are two unresolved data-quality threads now in their second week running: a counterfactual ledger that has recorded zero closes ever, with positions now past the primary book's own hold-time ceiling; and a symbol flagged twice against an identical witness price, which reads like a checkable data bug rather than two unrelated anomalies. Neither is a trading-logic fault, but both are concrete things to verify before the next report repeats them a third time. The sample is also still small (34 of 200 all-time) -- directional, not conclusive, even setting the above aside.
